quizzes.question: Indian mathematician Radhanath Sikdar first calculated the position of this geographical feature as the world's highest peak in 1852. Known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, its dangerous upper region above 8,000 meters is designated as the Death Zone. First summiting on May 29, 1953, Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first confirmed people to reach its peak. For the point, name this highest mountain on Earth, located in the Himalayas.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest, located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and China, was first identified as Earth's highest peak by Radhanath Sikdar and first summitted by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: The centripetal form of this vector quantity is directed toward the center of a circular path and equals velocity squared divided by radius. On a velocity-versus-time graph, the slope of the curve represents this value, while the area under the curve gives displacement. Measured in meters per second squared, it is defined by Newton's Second Law as force divided by mass. For the point, name this rate of change of an object's velocity over time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m/s², and represents the slope on a velocity-vs-time graph.

quizzes.question: Rising roughly 4 millimeters per year due to tectonic uplift, this peak is situated in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. Named after a former Surveyor General of India, its summit elevation was officially measured at 8,848.86 meters above sea level. It sits directly on the international border between Nepal and China. For the point, name this mountain, the highest peak in the world.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest continues to rise due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates and holds the highest peak elevation above sea level at 8,848.86 meters.

quizzes.question: Albert Einstein's Theory of General Relativity redefines this interaction as a consequence of mass warping the four-dimensional fabric of spacetime. Despite being the weakest of the four fundamental interactions, it dictates large-scale cosmic structure and ocean tides because it is purely attractive and has an infinite range. Its classical magnitude is proportional to the product of two masses divided by the square of the distance between them. For the point, name this attractive force that causes objects to accelerate toward Earth at roughly 9.81 m/s².
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is the fundamental attractive interaction between masses governed classically by Newton's inverse-square law and relativistically by general relativity.

quizzes.question: Climbers attempting the Southeast Ridge route on this mountain must traverse the hazardous Khumbu Icefall and pass through the South Col. Situated in the Mahalangur Himal, its high altitude forces climbers in the Death Zone to use supplemental oxygen due to extremely low atmospheric pressure. It was first successfully ascended in May 1953 by Sherpa climber Tenzing Norgay and New Zealander Edmund Hillary. For the point, name this famous Himalayan mountain on the Nepal-China border.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest features famous climbing locations such as the Khumbu Icefall and South Col, and its upper region requires supplemental oxygen due to low pressure.

quizzes.question: First published together in the 1687 landmark treatise Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, these three principles form the cornerstone of classical mechanics. The first of these principles is also known as the Law of Inertia, while the third asserts that every action force has an equal and opposite reaction. The second principle defines net force as equal to mass times acceleration. For the point, name these three fundamental physical laws formulated by an English scientist.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion were published in the Principia Mathematica in 1687 and establish fundamental classical relationships involving inertia, acceleration (F=ma), and action-reaction pairs.

quizzes.question: During the Great Trigonometrical Survey, this geographical feature was designated as Peak XV before being renamed in honor of a British Surveyor General of India. Known locally in Nepal as Sagarmatha, it is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent of this peak in 1953. For the point, name this highest peak above sea level on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Formerly designated Peak XV, Mount Everest was renamed after Sir George Everest, former Surveyor General of India, and is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal.

quizzes.question: C4 and CAM plants utilize specialized structural adaptations to minimize photorespiration during this metabolic process, which fixes carbon using the enzyme RuBisCO. Its light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts, generating ATP and NADPH while photolysis splits water into oxygen. This biological process allows autotrophs to convert solar light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into chemical energy stored as glucose. For the point, name this process by which green plants produce oxygen.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in plant chloroplasts, utilizing light reactions in thylakoids and carbon fixation via RuBisCO in the Calvin cycle to yield glucose and oxygen.

quizzes.question: The ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates causes this mountain peak to grow approximately 4 millimeters higher each year. Straddling the international border of Nepal and the Tibetan region of China, its upper regions above 8,000 meters suffer from atmospheric pressure too low to sustain human life without oxygen assistance. It was first summited in 1953 by Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary. For the point, name this Himalayan mountain that stands at 8,848.86 meters.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest's height of 8,848.86 meters is maintained and uplifted by tectonic activity between the Indian and Eurasian plates.

quizzes.question: Local variations in this force occur across Earth's surface due to differences in altitude, latitude, and sub-surface geological mass distribution. Its universal constant, denoted by a capital G, is approximately 6.674 times 10 to the power of negative 11 N·m²/kg². Classically formulated by Sir Isaac Newton, this attractive interaction governs planetary orbits and creates ocean tides. For the point, name this fundamental force responsible for weight, which causes unsupported objects to fall toward Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is determined by Newton's constant G, causing objects to have weight and fall toward Earth while also driving orbital mechanics and ocean tides.

quizzes.question: Indian mathematician Radhanath Sikdar was the first to calculate the position and height of this geographical feature in 1852. Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range, it is known locally as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, and its upper zone above 8,000 meters is famously called the Death Zone. Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first confirmed people to reach its summit in 1953. For the point, name this highest mountain peak on Earth above sea level.
quizzes.explanation: Radhanath Sikdar first calculated the height of Mount Everest in 1852. Known as Sagarmatha and Chomolungma, it features the Death Zone above 8,000 meters and was first summitted by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: The first publication detailing these three fundamental principles appeared in the 1687 landmark treatise Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica. The first of these principles introduces the concept of inertia, while the third states that every action produces an equal and opposite reaction. The second principle defines force as mass times acceleration, traditionally written as F equals m a. For the point, name these three fundamental laws of physical mechanics formulated by an English scientist.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion were published in the Principia Mathematica in 1687 and lay the groundwork for classical mechanics through concepts of inertia, F=ma, and action-reaction pairs.

quizzes.question: Rising roughly 4 millimeters each year due to the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates, this landform was named after a former Surveyor General of India. Climbers ascending its standard route must navigate treacherous hazards such as the Khumbu Icefall while managing the risks of severe atmospheric pressure drop. Straddling the international border between Nepal and China, its peak reaches an official elevation of over 8,848 meters. For the point, name this peak located in the Himalayas, the tallest mountain in the world.
quizzes.explanation: Named after Sir George Everest, Mount Everest continues to rise due to the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plate collision and straddles the border of Nepal and China in the Himalayas.

quizzes.question: Centripetal forms of this physical quantity describe motion directed toward the center of a circular path using the formula v squared over r. Represented as the slope on a velocity-versus-time graph, it is a vector quantity measured in meters per second squared in the SI system. Standard Earth surface values for this quantity due to gravity are represented by the symbol g and equal approximately 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this physics term defined as the rate of change of velocity over time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration measures the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, has SI units of m/s², and represents the slope of a velocity-time graph.

quizzes.question: The region above 8,000 meters on this mountain is known as the Death Zone because human life cannot be sustained there over extended periods without supplemental oxygen. Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range, it was first successfully summitted on May 29, 1953. A Sherpa climber from Nepal named Tenzing Norgay reached its summit alongside a climber from New Zealand. For the point, name this mountain whose top was reached by Sir Edmund Hillary.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest's upper extreme altitude is known as the Death Zone. On May 29, 1953, Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay completed the first confirmed successful summit ascent.

quizzes.question: Specialized C4 and CAM plants utilize anatomical adaptations to minimize photorespiration by separating initial carbon fixation from the rest of this biological pathway. Its light-dependent stage takes place in thylakoid membranes, where photolysis splits water to produce oxygen while generating ATP and NADPH. The light-independent Calvin cycle relies on the abundant enzyme RuBisCO to process carbon dioxide into glucose. For the point, name this process used by autotrophs to convert light energy into chemical energy.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis consists of thylakoid light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle, utilizing RuBisCO to fix carbon dioxide and create chemical energy from light.

quizzes.question: The surveyor Radhanath Sikdar initially identified this geographic feature as Peak XV before it was renamed after a British Surveyor General. Formed by tectonic plate uplift in the Himalayas, its international border divides the Autonomous Region of Tibet from Nepal's Sagarmatha National Park. It is officially recognized as the highest point above sea level on Earth at an altitude of 29,031 feet. For the point, name this famous mountain on the border of Nepal and China.
quizzes.explanation: Originally designated Peak XV, Mount Everest sits on the border of Nepal and Tibet (China) in Sagarmatha National Park and stands as the highest point on Earth.

quizzes.question: Albert Einstein's Theory of General Relativity reinterprets this fundamental interaction not as a mechanical force, but as a consequence of mass warping the fabric of four-dimensional spacetime. Formulated classically by Isaac Newton, its magnitude is directly proportional to the product of two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. Although it is the weakest of the four fundamental forces, it governs planetary orbits and ocean tides. For the point, name this force that gives weight to physical objects and pulls them toward Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is modeled classically by Newton's inverse-square law and relativistically by Einstein's spacetime curvature, driving planetary orbits and surface gravity.

quizzes.question: In Tibet, this natural landmark is known as Chomolungma, meaning Goddess Mother of the World, while in Nepal it is called Sagarmatha. Climbers attempting to reach its peak usually pass through the South Col or North Ridge routes after departing from Base Camp. Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first verified adventurers to stand atop its highest point in 1953. For the point, name this Asian mountain that stands as the world's highest peak.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is called Chomolungma in Tibet and Sagarmatha in Nepal. Its primary climbing routes pass through South Col and North Ridge from Base Camp.

quizzes.question: The second of these principles states that net force equals mass times acceleration, which can also be expressed as the rate of change of momentum over time. The first principle dictates that an object in motion will remain in motion unless acted upon by a net external force. The third principle asserts that whenever one object exerts a force on another, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first. For the point, name these three physical laws named after the English author of Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica.
quizzes.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton formulated these three laws of motion, which govern inertia, net force with acceleration (F=ma), and action-reaction pairs.
